messages.subject: Overlay histogram
parts:
Hi! I would like to overlay three histograms with ggplot, using
different colors and alpha. There is something like here
http://stackoverflow.com/questions/6957549/overlaying-histograms-with-ggplot2-in-r
but I can't figure out how to apply to my data.

Bellow are the codes for the individuals histograms.

ggplot(data=elev, aes(x=elev_carta)) + geom_histogram(binwidth=50)
ggplot(data=elev, aes(x=elev_aster)) + geom_histogram(binwidth=50)
ggplot(data=elev, aes(x=elev_srtm)) + geom_histogram(binwidth=50)

--
Regards,

messages.author: d31339b95f6e694c
messages.subject: Re: Overlay histogram
parts:
On 2012-Apr-16, at 15:08 , Brandon Hurr wrote:
>
> ggplot(data=elev) +
>
>
> geom_histogram

> (aes(x=elev_carta), fill = "red", alpha = 0.2) +
>
>
> geom_histogram
> (aes(x=elev_aster), fill = "blue", alpha = 0.2) +
>
>
>
> geom_histogram(aes(x=elev_srtm), fill = "green", alpha = 0.2)
>
> Something like that maybe. Hard to say without your data or a reproducible example.

This would work, but "the ggplot way" would rather be to have all the data in a single data.frame and use aes(colour=something). This has the side effect of stacking the bars on top of each other. You have to counteract this by setting position="identity"

Example (which the original poster should have provided, indeed):

d <- data.frame(kind=rep(c("a", "b", "c"), each=100), x=c(rnorm(100, 1), rnorm(100, 2), rnorm(100, 3)))
library("ggplot2")
# base histogram, the bars are stacked on top of each other
ggplot() + geom_histogram(aes(x=x, fill=kind), data=d, binwidth=0.2)
# shift the bars relative to each other (=dodging) i.e. what other software (Excel, ...) usually does
ggplot() + geom_histogram(aes(x=x, fill=kind), data=d, binwidth=0.2, position="dodge")
# superpose the bars
ggplot() + geom_histogram(aes(x=x, fill=kind), data=d, binwidth=0.2, position="identity")
# except that, if you want to see something, you have to use trasnparency
ggplot() + geom_histogram(aes(x=x, fill=kind), data=d, binwidth=0.2, position="identity", alpha=0.5, colour=scales::alpha("black", 0.2))

# but I'd say this is messy and difficult to read, in that configuration, using a density estimate provides a better, more readable graph I think
ggplot() + geom_density(aes(x=x, fill=kind), data=d, binwidth=0.2, position="identity", alpha=0.5, colour=scales::alpha("black", 0.2))

Jean-Olivier Irisson

messages.author: 5f8b51633aa2f2a1
messages.subject: Re: Overlay histogram
parts:
One of the easiest ways (for reasonably sized data sets) is to use
dput() -- it will create a plain text representation of your data that
can be included inline so you don't have to worry about mail servers
scrubbing attachments; then your correspondents can just copy and
paste it directly into an R session to reproduce your data.

Michael
